text:
maria: Anyone seeing GPU node boot failures in eu-central after the nightly janitor run? provisioner keeps timing out waiting for scratch disk attach.

sam: yep, got a pile of evicts and failed mounts. dmesg shows repeated nvme retries and heavy writeback stalls.

alex: paste a log snippet?

sam: ```
[ 1234.567890] nvme0: I/O error, opcode 0x02, status 0x8
[ 1234.568001] nvme_core: read amplification ratio=4.2, io_queued=512, writeback_backlog_ms=220
[ 1234.568102] blk_update_request: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, sector 12345678
```

infra-bot: :warning: alert: eu-central nvme_io_surge detected (35 nodes), severity=medium, triggered_by=janitor-scrub

lee: hypothesis: scrub/trim job overlapped with heavy batch provisioning. controllers doing compaction and causing GC IOPS spike -> kernel qdepth blowout.

maria: agree. scrub window is 02:00-03:00 UTC which is our provisioning peak for some eu-central customers. We should throttle or shift.

sam: quick mitigation: disable scrub for pool eu-central-scratch for 30m and set per-device throttle to 1000 iops for scrub threads. also mark nodes to avoid new GPU scheduling.

alex: how do we mark nodes? can we add a scheduling taint/label so provisioner skips them?

maria: doing canary now: `kubectl label node gnode-345 avoid-provisioning=true` and patched janitor config to reduce concurrency to 2 for eu-central.

infra-bot: action: scrub_disabled pool=eu-central-scratch duration=30m by=maria at=1713456795

sam: spinning up SMART telemetry collectors for those drives and capturing ioheatmap for last 6h. also added `echo 200 > /sys/block/nvme0n1/queue/nr_requests` on a few canaries to limit qdepth.

lee: if this recovers, we should add a scheduling policy to provisioner to prefer nodes with iops_headroom > 30% and avoid starting scrubs when pending GPU boot_count > 5.

maria: agreed. if we don't see mount recovery in 15m we'll revert scrub and failover some capacity to us-west2 to keep SLAs. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

alex: noted. i'll open a quick runbook PR for on-call steps and add a dashboard panel for scrub overlap with provisioning.

sam: observed reduced writeback latency on canary after throttle. mounts coming back on 6/35 nodes. continuing to monitor.

maria: thanks. leave this thread pinned to eu-central incident channel until fully stable.

infra-bot: note: action logged scrub_reenable: scheduled at=1713458595 pool=eu-central-scratch (pending)
